correctness.rationale: A subset of a complete multipartite graph is total dominating exactly when it meets at least two parts. With at least three represented parts, replacing a defender can remove at most one represented part, so security is automatic. With exactly two parts \(X_i,X_j\), an omitted vertex of \(X_i\) is defensible exactly when \(X_i\) is already full or at least two selected vertices remain in \(X_j\), and symmetrically. This proves the support criterion, from which the enumerator and minimum cases follow by direct counting. An independent definition-level brute-force recheck matched the criterion on representative multipartite profiles.
